newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria adopts a new privatisation law.
newsitem.headline: Algeria adopts a new privatisation law.

text.p: Algeria's government-appointed Transitional National Council (CNT) on Sunday passed a new privatisation law to woo investors to buy into ailing state-owned firms.

The official Algerian news agency APS said the CNT, a quasi parliament, altered the landmark 1995 privatisation law to promise incentives to investors who save jobs and upgrade the firms they acquire.
Incentives include tax deductions and easy loans. The change scraps the prior provision that new owners keep on all the workers.
The new law also scraps compulsory cash payment, replacing it by sales on deferred terms.
The government is expected soon to offer more than 250 state-owned firms and industrial units for sale to private investors.

Privatisation has been a thorny issue in Algeria, where officials fear massive lay-offs of workers stemming from a speedy sell-off might fan the five years of civil strife. during its transition to a fully fledged free market economy.

The government, which is trying to move to a full market economy, has tried to play down the lack of interest in privatisation, in which only 10 of more than 70 enterprises offered for sale have found takers.

Algeria has been battered by violence in the past five years during which about 60,000 people have died. Officials blame poverty, jobless and lack of houses for driving many disgruntled young people into the arms of Moslem fundamentalist guerrillas trying to topple the government.
Economists said the requirements in the 1995 laws had kept investors at bay.
